title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance and Manager Guide (2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard hiring processes, new-hire onboarding plan, performance and feedback cycles, and practical guidance for managers. It is intended to be the canonical reference for people managers and People Ops partners.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contract employees hired in 2025-2027.
- Includes steps owned by hiring managers, recruiting, People Ops, IT, and security.

Table of contents
-----------------
1. Hiring process overview
2. Interview and evaluation standards
3. Offer and background checks
4. Onboarding (first 90 days) and checklist
5. Performance cycles and calibration
6. Manager playbook: 1:1s, feedback, career conversations, PIPs
7. Roles and ownership
8. Templates and links

1) Hiring process overview
-------------------------
Intro: Our goal is to hire reliably for skill, mission alignment, and long-term potential while creating a predictable candidate experience that reflects Redwood's values. Time-to-offer and interview quality are tracked as metrics.

Key stages (high level):
- Requisition & role definition (Hiring manager + People Ops)
- Sourcing & outreach (Recruiting)
- Screening (Recruiter phone screen)
- Technical / functional interviews (Hiring team)
- Final onsite / loop (4-5 interviewers where applicable)
- Hiring debrief & calibration (Hiring manager + interviewers + Recruiting)
- Offer (Hiring manager + People Ops)
- Acceptance, background checks, and start-date coordination

SLOs and metrics:
- Target time-to-offer: 28 days from req approval to offer (metric: median)
- Target interview-to-offer conversion: 25% (role dependent)
- Candidate NPS target: 60+

Requisition checklist (required before sourcing):
- Approved headcount and budget confirmation (Finance + Hiring manager)
- Role description with clear responsibilities and success metrics
- Compensation band and target level (People Ops comp partner)
- Interview rubric draft aligned to role (see section 2)

2) Interview and evaluation standards
----------------------------------
Principles: structured interviews, calibrated rubrics, diverse panels, and documented feedback. Hiring decisions are evidence-based.

Interview types and owners:
- Recruiter screen (30 min): fit, compensation expectations, basic skills - Recruiting
- Technical deep-dive (45-60 min): systems, algorithms, design, or coding - Hiring team engineering
- Take-home or pair programming (role-dependent) - Hiring team
- Leadership / cross-functional (30-45 min): collaboration, decision-making, influence - Hiring manager and cross-team partner

Evaluation rubric (required fields for each interviewer):
- Technical competence: scale 1-5 (examples of evidence)
- Problem-solving approach: 1-5 (communication, tradeoffs)
- Role-specific skills: 1-5 (domain knowledge)
- Collaboration & culture add: 1-5 (ownership, communication)
- Overall recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / No Hire / Hold

Calibration guidance: before debrief, reviewers must submit written notes. Hiring manager consolidates and schedules a short calibration session (max 30 min) to discuss discrepant ratings. Hiring managers may reach out to People Ops for tie-breaking guidance on borderline cases.

Diversity & fairness: include at least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing for senior roles. Avoid single-interviewer decisions for levels above IC3. Ensure job postings use inclusive language.

3) Offer and background checks
--------------------------------
Offer approval flow:
1. Hiring manager proposes salary within band and bonus/eq (if applicable).
2. People Ops verifies comp alignment and prepares offer letter.
3. Legal/Finance review for managers and senior ICs (L5+).
4. Recruiter extends verbal offer; People Ops sends official offer letter.

Offer components to include in the letter:
- Role title and level
- Compensation (base salary, bonus targets, equity grants or RSU plan summary)
- Benefits summary and eligibility date
- Start date and location (remote/on-site expectations)
- Contingencies: background check, right-to-work verification

Background checks and compliance:
- Standard background check (criminal, employment verification) is initiated after verbal acceptance.
- Certain customers/roles require enhanced checks and must be flagged at req creation.
- People Ops owns vendor relationship; hiring manager ensures any role-specific check requirements are documented.

Offer rescind policy: Offers can be rescinded only in documented circumstances (fraudulent information, failed checks). People Ops and Legal must be involved.

4) Onboarding: first 90 days and checklist
----------------------------------------
Onboarding philosophy: fast time-to-productivity while creating clarity on expectations, culture, and support networks. Onboarding is a shared responsibility across People Ops, IT, manager, and mentor/buddy.

First-day essentials (owned items):
- People Ops: Welcome email, benefits enrollment packet, access to HRIS (Paylocity/Greenhouse integration notes).
- IT: Laptop provisioned and imaged, VPN access, SSO account setup, MFA enabled.
- Security: Required training links (security awareness), onboarding security checklist.
- Manager: 1:1 scheduled, team intro meeting, first-week plan.

30/60/90 day plan (manager templated objectives):
- Day 0-7: Orientation, learn docs, complete mandatory trainings, set up dev environment, meet direct team.
- 30 days: Deliver small onboarding project or docs update; demonstrate ability to run simple workflows independently.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a modest feature or operational responsibility; participate in cross-team meetings.
- 90 days: Goal alignment conversation; identify impact goals for next 6-12 months.

New hire checklist (quick reference):
- Pre-boarding: signed offer, background check initiated, equipment order placed, manager welcome email sent.
- Day 0: account provisioning, Slack invite, Jira/Confluence access, code repo access request filed.
- Week 1: team orientation, review role objectives, first 1:1, mentor assigned.
- Month 1-3: 30/60/90 checkpoints, learning plan, career development meeting.

Sample onboarding table (manager-visible)
| Item | Owner | Due |
|------|-------|-----|
| Equipment delivered and tested | IT | Day 0 |
| Security training completed | New hire | Day 3 |
| First code review contribution | New hire | Day 30 |
| 30-day check-in | Manager | Day 30 |
| 90-day performance alignment | Manager + People Ops | Day 90 |

Buddy program: Assign a peer buddy for the first 90 days to help with tooling, culture, and domain questions. Buddies should check in weekly for the first month and biweekly until day 90.

5) Performance cycles and calibration
-------------------------------------
Cycle cadence:
- Annual performance cycle: goal-setting (Q1), mid-year review (end of Q2), annual review (Q4).
- Ongoing feedback: continuous, documented in performance system.
- Calibration windows: mid-year and year-end to normalize ratings.

Goal setting guidance:
- Use OKR-style goals where applicable: 3-5 objectives with measurable key results or success criteria.
- Managers should set initial goals with new hires within the first 30 days (informal) and finalize by 45 days.

Review types and workflow:
- Self-assessment (employee): narrative + evidence (projects, metrics).
- Manager assessment: strengths, areas for growth, rating on standard scale (Exceeds / Meets / Partially Meets / Below).
- Skip-level input and peer feedback: collected via the performance system for senior roles.
- Calibration: managers present assessments and supporting evidence to a calibration committee (People Ops facilitates).

Rating definitions (summary):
- Exceeds Expectations: consistently delivers above defined goals; measurable, replicable impact.
- Meets Expectations: reliably meets objectives; demonstrates required competencies.
- Partially Meets Expectations: inconsistent delivery; needs regular coaching.
- Below Expectations: does not meet core responsibilities; consider a performance improvement plan (PIP).

Compensation & promotions timing:
- Salary increases and bonus adjustments are tied to the annual cycle and promotion events. Off-cycle promotions are permitted for strong, well-documented cases and require People Ops approval.

6) Manager playbook: 1:1s, feedback, career conversations, PIPs
---------------------------------------------------------------
Regular manager practices:
- 1:1 cadence: weekly 30-60 minute meetings for direct reports. Agenda should be shared in advance.
- Check-in template (recommended): Wins, Roadblocks, Priorities, Career/Development items, Action items.
- Feedback rhythm: give public recognition for wins and private, specific corrective feedback as soon as possible. Use the SBI model (Situation, Behavior, Impact).

Career conversations:
- Quarterly career conversations: review career goals, mapped competencies, and potential stretch assignments.
- Use the career ladder for role expectations and to set promotion readiness milestones.

Performance Improvement Plans (PIP):
- Trigger conditions: sustained Partially / Below Expectations rating after coaching or repeated missed commitments.
- PIP components: clear expectations, success metrics, timeline (typically 60-90 days), weekly manager check-ins, and People Ops oversight.
- Outcomes: successful (return to regular cycle + potential compensation considerations) or unsuccessful (may lead to termination; Legal and People Ops must be involved).

Difficult conversations template (for managers):
1. Prepare: gather facts and examples.
2. State the issue: specific behaviors and impacts.
3. Share expectations: what success looks like.
4. Co-create plan: actions, support, timelines.
5. Document: write a summary and share next steps.

7) Roles and ownership
----------------------
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview loop design, final hiring decision, onboarding owner.
- Recruiting: sourcing, initial screens, candidate experience.
- People Ops: comp approvals, offer letters, background checks, process owner for performance cycles.
- IT & Security: account provisioning, device management, security training.
- Mentor/Buddy: day-to-day support during onboarding.

Escalation matrix (common issues):
- Offer disputes or comp exceptions: People Ops -> Finance -> EVP People for escalations.
- Background check delays: Recruiting -> People Ops -> Vendor.
- Onboarding access problems: Manager -> IT ticketing -> Eng Platform SRE if system outage.

Appendix: Quick CLI/IT checklist for managers
------------------------------------------------
- To request additional repos or infra access: open ticket in ServiceDesk with: employee name, role, repos/teams, justification, approval by manager.
- To order equipment: Use IT portal and select "New hire - Standard Mac" or "Standard Linux dev box". Allow 7 business days for procurement.

Frequently asked questions
--------------------------
Q: When should I start recruiting for a backfilled role?
A: Start the requisition process as soon as the headcount is confirmed; do not wait for an official resignation date.

Q: How do I request an off-cycle promotion?
A: Document contributions, manager recommendation, and comp rationale; submit to People Ops for review.

Q: Who owns compliance for international hires?
A: People Ops coordinates with Legal and local payroll partners to verify work eligibility and tax treatment.
